title: 17 — Angular & TypeScript Deep Dive
html:
17 — Angular & TypeScript Deep Dive

Scope: the type system beneath your code, and the framework mechanics (change detection, signals, RxJS, rendering) that determine whether an Angular app is fast and maintainable or slow and tangled.

1. TypeScript: the parts that pay off

1.1 Structural typing

TypeScript checks shape, not name. Two independently-declared types with the same members are interchangeable. This is why "it compiles" doesn't mean "it's the thing you meant" — and why branded types matter:

// ❌ Both are just `string` — the compiler cannot help you
function transfer(from: string, to: string, amount: number) {}
transfer(accountB, accountA, 100);          // silently wrong

// ✔ Branded (nominal-ish) types
type Brand<T, B extends string> = T & { readonly __brand: B };
type AccountId  = Brand<string, 'AccountId'>;
type PortfolioId = Brand<string, 'PortfolioId'>;

const asAccountId = (v: string): AccountId => v as AccountId;

function transfer(from: AccountId, to: AccountId, amount: number) {}
// transfer(portfolioId, accountId, 100);   // ← compile error. The bug is now impossible.

1.2 Configuration that actually matters

{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true,                              // the umbrella — turn it on
    "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true,            // arr[i] is T | undefined. Catches real bugs
    "exactOptionalPropertyTypes": true,          // { a?: string } ≠ { a: undefined }
    "noImplicitOverride": true,
    "noFallthroughCasesInSwitch": true,
    "noUnusedLocals": true,
    "useUnknownInCatchVariables": true,          // catch (e: unknown) — forces narrowing
    "isolatedModules": true
  },
  "angularCompilerOptions": {
    "strictTemplates": true,                     // type-checks bindings in templates
    "strictInjectionParameters": true
  }
}

⚠️ strictTemplates is the highest-value Angular-specific flag. Without it, template expressions are effectively untyped and your "strict" TypeScript stops at the component boundary.

1.3 any vs unknown vs never

Type Meaning Use
any Disables checking. Contagious Never in new code. Each any is a hole in the whole graph
unknown "I don't know yet" — must narrow before use External data, catch variables, generic boundaries
never Impossible Exhaustiveness checks, functions that always throw 
// Exhaustiveness: adding a new status becomes a COMPILE error, not a runtime surprise
function label(status: TradeStatus): string {
  switch (status) {
    case 'draft':    return 'Draft';
    case 'approved': return 'Approved';
    case 'settled':  return 'Settled';
    default: {
      const exhaustive: never = status;
      throw new Error(`Unhandled status: ${exhaustive}`);
    }
  }
}

1.4 Discriminated unions — make illegal states unrepresentable

type RequestState<T> =
  | { status: 'idle' }
  | { status: 'loading' }
  | { status: 'success'; data: T }
  | { status: 'error'; error: ApiError };

// The compiler now guarantees you can't read `data` while loading,
// and the template can't render an error message on success.

This single pattern eliminates the classic isLoading && !error && data boolean soup and the "flash of empty state" bugs that come with it.

1.5 Utility and advanced types worth knowing

Partial<T> Required<T> Readonly<T> Pick<T,K> Omit<T,K> Record<K,V>
ReturnType<F> Parameters<F> Awaited<P> NonNullable<T> Extract<T,U> Exclude<T,U>

// Deep readonly for immutable state
type DeepReadonly<T> = { readonly [K in keyof T]: T[K] extends object ? DeepReadonly<T[K]> : T[K] };

// Runtime validation at the boundary — types don't exist at runtime, so validate what crosses in
const PortfolioSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string().uuid(),
  name: z.string().min(1),
  holdings: z.array(z.object({ code: z.string(), weight: z.number().min(0).max(1) })),
});
type Portfolio = z.infer<typeof PortfolioSchema>;   // one source of truth for type AND validation

⚠️ A TypeScript interface over an HTTP response is a hope, not a check. The API can return anything. Validate at the boundary (zod/valibot) or accept that a schema change becomes a runtime undefined is not a function in production.

2. Angular architecture

2.1 Standalone-first (modern Angular)

@Component({
  selector: 'app-portfolio-list',
  standalone: true,                                   // default in v19+
  imports: [AsyncPipe, RouterLink, CurrencyPipe],     // explicit, tree-shakeable
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,    // default for new components
  template: `
    @if (vm(); as model) {
      <table>
        @for (row of model.rows; track row.id) {
          <tr><td>{{ row.name }}</td><td>{{ row.value | currency:'GBP' }}</td></tr>
        } @empty {
          <tr><td colspan="2">No portfolios found.</td></tr>
        }
      </table>
    } @else {
      <app-spinner />
    }
  `,
})
export class PortfolioListComponent {
  private readonly service = inject(PortfolioService);
  protected readonly vm = toSignal(this.service.viewModel$);
}

⚠️ Never mix standalone and NgModule styles arbitrarily in one codebase. Pick the project's existing convention; migrating is a deliberate, whole-app decision.

2.2 Layering

Components (dumb where possible: inputs in, outputs out, no HTTP, no business rules)
    ↓
Facades / feature services (state + orchestration)
    ↓
Data services (HttpClient only, typed, one per API resource)
    ↓
Interceptors (auth, correlation, retry, error mapping)

Rules: no HttpClient in a component; no business rules in a template; smart (container) components fetch and coordinate, presentational components take inputs and emit outputs. This is what makes components testable without a TestBed.

2.3 Folder structure that scales

src/app/
  core/           # singletons: interceptors, guards, app-wide services, config
  shared/         # dumb components, pipes, directives, no feature knowledge
  features/
    portfolios/
      data/       # services, models, mappers
      ui/         # presentational components
      pages/      # routed containers
      portfolios.routes.ts
  app.routes.ts

Enforce boundaries with ESLint (eslint-plugin-boundaries or Nx tags): shared must not import features; features must not import each other directly.

3. Change detection — the mechanism

3.1 The old model (Zone.js)

Zone.js monkey-patches every async API (setTimeout, addEventListener, XHR, promises). When any of them fires, Angular runs change detection over the entire component tree, re-evaluating every template binding.

With Default change detection, a single mousemove handler somewhere triggers a full tree check. On a large app that's thousands of expression evaluations per event.

3.2 OnPush

changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush

The component is checked only when:

  1. An @Input() reference changes (reference equality — mutating an object in place does not trigger it),
  2. An event originates from the component or its template,
  3. An async pipe in its template emits,
  4. markForCheck() is called explicitly,
  5. A signal read in its template changes.

OnPush + immutable data is the standard performance posture. ⚠️ The most common OnPush bug: mutating an array (this.items.push(x)) instead of replacing it (this.items = [...this.items, x]) — the view silently doesn't update.

3.3 Signals (the modern model)

Signals make change detection fine-grained: Angular tracks exactly which templates read which signals, and updates only those — no tree traversal.

export class PortfolioComponent {
  // state
  readonly holdings = signal<Holding[]>([]);
  readonly filter   = signal('');

  // derived — recomputed lazily, memoised, only when a dependency changes
  readonly filtered = computed(() =>
    this.holdings().filter(h => h.code.includes(this.filter().toUpperCase())));

  readonly total = computed(() =>
    this.filtered().reduce((sum, h) => sum + h.marketValue, 0));

  // side effects — NOT for deriving state
  constructor() {
    effect(() => console.debug('Filter changed to', this.filter()));
  }

  updateFilter(value: string): void {
    this.filter.set(value);
  }

  addHolding(h: Holding): void {
    this.holdings.update(current => [...current, h]);   // new reference
  }
}
Primitive Purpose Warning
signal() Writable state —
computed() Derived, memoised, lazy Must be pure — no side effects, no HTTP
effect() Reacts to changes for side effects ⚠️ Not for deriving state; runs after render; easy to create loops
linkedSignal() Writable state derived from a source v19+
toSignal() / toObservable() RxJS interop toSignal needs an initialValue or emits undefined first
input() / output() / model() Signal-based component I/O Replaces @Input/@Output decorators
resource() / httpResource() Async data as a signal with loading/error state v19/v20

Signals vs RxJS — how to choose:

Use signals for Use RxJS for
Synchronous component/UI state Streams of events over time
Derived values HTTP with retry/cancel/switch semantics
Template bindings Debouncing, throttling, buffering
Simple state that "is a value" Complex async coordination, websockets

They interoperate; the pragmatic pattern is RxJS at the edges (HTTP, websockets, events) → toSignal → signals in the component and template.

3.4 Zoneless

bootstrapApplication(AppComponent, {
  providers: [provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection()]   // name varies by version
});

Removes Zone.js entirely (~13 KB, and the monkey-patching overhead). Requires that everything driving UI updates is a signal or an explicit markForCheck. Migration path: OnPush everywhere → signals for state → async pipe or toSignal for observables → then go zoneless.

4. RxJS — operator selection

The mental model: an Observable is a lazy stream. Nothing happens until you subscribe; each subscription runs the producer again (unless it's shared/multicast).

4.1 The flattening operators (the one thing to get right)

Operator On a new inner emission Use for
switchMap Cancels the previous inner Typeahead, route params, any "latest wins" request. Default choice for HTTP reads
concatMap Queues; runs in order Sequential writes where order matters
mergeMap Runs all concurrently Independent parallel work (bound it with the concurrency arg)
exhaustMap Ignores new while one is in flight Save/submit buttons — prevents duplicate submissions

⚠️ Using mergeMap for a search-as-you-type produces out-of-order responses: you type "abc", the response for "ab" arrives after the one for "abc", and the UI shows the wrong results. switchMap is the fix. ⚠️ Using switchMap for a POST cancels an in-flight write — the request may still have reached the server. Use concatMap or exhaustMap for writes.

// Typeahead done correctly
readonly results$ = this.searchControl.valueChanges.pipe(
  debounceTime(300),
  map(v => v?.trim() ?? ''),
  distinctUntilChanged(),
  filter(term => term.length === 0 || term.length >= 2),
  switchMap(term => term
    ? this.api.search(term).pipe(catchError(() => of([])))   // inner catch keeps the outer alive
    : of([])),
  shareReplay({ bufferSize: 1, refCount: true }),
);

⚠️ catchError on the outer stream kills it permanently. After an error, the source completes and never emits again — the search box stops working. Always catch inside the inner observable. This is the single most common RxJS bug in Angular apps.

4.2 Subscription management

export class LiveComponent {
  private readonly destroyRef = inject(DestroyRef);

  constructor() {
    // ✔ Auto-unsubscribes on destroy
    this.socket.messages$
      .pipe(takeUntilDestroyed(this.destroyRef))
      .subscribe(m => this.handle(m));
  }
}

Preference order: async pipe (no manual subscription at all) > toSignal() > takeUntilDestroyed() > manual Subscription + ngOnDestroy. ⚠️ A subscribe() with no teardown in a component that's created/destroyed repeatedly (a routed page, a list item) is a memory leak and a source of duplicate HTTP calls.

4.3 Multicasting

HttpClient observables are cold and complete after one emission, so multiple async pipes on the same observable trigger multiple HTTP requests. Fix with shareReplay({ bufferSize: 1, refCount: true }) — and use refCount: true so the cache is released when the last subscriber leaves (without it, shareReplay holds the value and the source subscription forever — a subtle leak).

4.4 Common patterns

// Combine dependent sources into a single view model — one subscription, one template guard
readonly vm$ = combineLatest({
  portfolio: this.route.paramMap.pipe(
    map(p => p.get('id')!),
    switchMap(id => this.api.getPortfolio(id)),
  ),
  prices: this.prices.live$,
  user: this.auth.currentUser$,
}).pipe(
  map(({ portfolio, prices, user }) => buildViewModel(portfolio, prices, user)),
  shareReplay({ bufferSize: 1, refCount: true }),
);

⚠️ combineLatest emits nothing until every source has emitted at least once. A source that never emits silently blocks the whole view — give each one a startWith.

5. Forms

Typed reactive forms only in new code.

private readonly fb = inject(NonNullableFormBuilder);

readonly form = this.fb.group({
  instrumentCode: this.fb.control('', [Validators.required, Validators.pattern(/^[A-Z0-9.]{1,12}$/)]),
  notional:       this.fb.control(0,  [Validators.required, Validators.min(0.01)]),
  tradeDate:      this.fb.control<Date | null>(null, Validators.required),
}, { validators: [tradeDateNotInFuture] });

submit(): void {
  if (this.form.invalid) { this.form.markAllAsTouched(); return; }
  const value = this.form.getRawValue();          // fully typed, includes disabled controls
  this.api.createTrade(value).subscribe(...);
}
Concern Approach
Cross-field rules A validator on the FormGroup, not on individual controls
Async validation asyncValidators with debounceTime + switchMap; show a pending state
Reusable field components Implement ControlValueAccessor, or take the FormControl as an input (simpler and usually better)
Dynamic forms FormArray with typed controls; always trackBy/track in the template
Disabled controls Excluded from value — use getRawValue()
Server validation errors Map API field errors back onto controls with setErrors

⚠️ Never validate only on the client. Client validation is UX; the server is the authority (file 13 §6).

6. HTTP and interceptors

export const authInterceptor: HttpInterceptorFn = (req, next) => {
  const auth = inject(AuthService);
  const correlationId = crypto.randomUUID();

  const cloned = req.clone({
    setHeaders: {
      ...(auth.token() ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${auth.token()}` } : {}),
      'X-Correlation-Id': correlationId,
    },
    withCredentials: true,
  });

  return next(cloned).pipe(
    retry({ count: 2, delay: (error, attempt) =>
      // Only retry idempotent requests on transient failures, with backoff
      req.method === 'GET' && error.status >= 500
        ? timer(300 * 2 ** attempt)
        : throwError(() => error) }),
    catchError((error: HttpErrorResponse) => {
      if (error.status === 401) auth.redirectToLogin();
      return throwError(() => toAppError(error, correlationId));
    }),
  );
};

bootstrapApplication(AppComponent, {
  providers: [provideHttpClient(withInterceptors([authInterceptor, loadingInterceptor]))],
});

Rules: typed responses (http.get<PortfolioDto[]>(...)); one data service per resource; map API DTOs to view models in the service, not the component; never build URLs by string concatenation with user input; use HttpParams for query strings.

7. Performance

7.1 Rendering

Technique Effect
OnPush everywhere Prunes the change-detection tree
track in @for Without it, Angular destroys and recreates every DOM node on any list change. Mandatory
@defer blocks Lazy-load a component subtree on viewport/interaction/timer — huge for below-the-fold content
Virtual scrolling (cdk-virtual-scroll) Render 20 rows instead of 20,000
Pure pipes over method calls in templates ⚠️ {{ calculateTotal() }} runs on every change-detection cycle
@let / memoised computed Avoid recomputing in the template
NgOptimizedImage Lazy loading, priority hints, correct sizing
runOutsideAngular Animation loops, third-party widgets, high-frequency events
Signals Fine-grained updates without tree traversal 
<!-- ❌ formatValue() runs on every CD cycle for every row -->
@for (row of rows; track row.id) { <td>{{ formatValue(row) }}</td> }

<!-- ✔ precompute in the view model, or use a pure pipe -->
@for (row of rows; track row.id) { <td>{{ row.formattedValue }}</td> }

7.2 Bundle size

// angular.json — budgets fail the build, which is the point
"budgets": [
  { "type": "initial", "maximumWarning": "500kB", "maximumError": "1MB" },
  { "type": "anyComponentStyle", "maximumWarning": "4kB" }
]
  • Lazy-load every feature route (loadComponent / loadChildren).
  • npx source-map-explorer dist/**/*.js — find what's actually big. Usually: moment.js, lodash imported whole, a chart library, or an icon set.
  • Import narrowly (import { debounce } from 'lodash-es', not import _ from 'lodash').
  • Prefer Intl and native Date APIs over date libraries.
  • Standalone components tree-shake better than NgModules.

7.3 Runtime measurement

Chrome DevTools Performance panel, Angular DevTools (component tree + change-detection profiler), Lighthouse for Core Web Vitals (LCP < 2.5 s, INP < 200 ms, CLS < 0.1). Measure on a throttled mid-tier device, not your workstation.

8. State management — choose the smallest thing that works

flowchart TD
    A[Where does this state live?] --> B{Used by one component?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Component signals]
    B -->|No| D{Shared by a few related components?}
    D -->|Yes| E[Feature service with signals/BehaviorSubject<br/>provided at the route level]
    D -->|No| F{App-wide, complex, needs<br/>time-travel/devtools/effects?}
    F -->|No| G[Root service with signals]
    F -->|Yes| H[NgRx SignalStore or NgRx Store]
    A --> I{Is it server data?}
    I -->|Yes| J[A query/cache layer:<br/>httpResource, TanStack Query,<br/>or a service with shareReplay]

The insight most teams miss: the majority of "state" in a typical app is server cache, not client state. Treating it as client state (copying it into a store, then keeping it in sync) creates most of the complexity. A caching data layer with invalidation is usually the better tool.

NgRx is justified when: many features share and mutate the same state, you need strict traceability of every change, or a large team benefits from the enforced structure. It is not justified for "we have a few shared values" — that's a service with signals.

9. Testing

Level Tool What
Unit (logic) Jest/Vitest, no TestBed Pure functions, services with mocked deps. Fast — most of your tests
Component TestBed + Testing Library Behaviour through the DOM: "when I click Save, the service is called"
HTTP HttpTestingController Assert request URL/method/body, flush responses
E2E Playwright/Cypress Critical journeys only — slow and flaky in bulk
Accessibility axe-core in CI Automated a11y regression checks
Visual Playwright screenshots / Chromatic Design-system components 
it('shows an error message when the API fails', async () => {
  await render(PortfolioListComponent, {
    providers: [{ provide: PortfolioService, useValue: { list: () => throwError(() => new Error()) } }],
  });
  expect(await screen.findByRole('alert')).toHaveTextContent(/could not load/i);
});

Principle: test behaviour through the public surface (rendered output and emitted events), never private methods. Tests that assert on internals break on every refactor and protect nothing.

10. Accessibility (non-negotiable, and frequently skipped)

  • Semantic HTML first. <button> over <div (click)> — you get keyboard, focus, and screen-reader support free.
  • Every input has a <label>; every image has alt; every icon-only button has aria-label.
  • Keyboard: every interactive element reachable and operable; visible focus indicator; logical tab order; Escape closes dialogs; focus trapped in modals and restored on close.
  • Announce dynamic changes with aria-live (loading states, validation errors, toasts).
  • Colour contrast ≥ 4.5:1; never convey information by colour alone.
  • Route changes should move focus and update the page title.
  • Use Angular CDK a11y utilities (FocusTrap, LiveAnnouncer, cdkTrapFocus).

11. Checklist & interview angles

Angular review checklist

  • strict + strictTemplates on; no any
  • OnPush (or signals/zoneless) on all components
  • track on every @for
  • No subscribe() without teardown; prefer async pipe or toSignal
  • catchError inside inner observables, not on the outer stream
  • Correct flattening operator (switchMap reads, exhaustMap/concatMap writes)
  • shareReplay({refCount: true}) on shared HTTP streams
  • No HTTP or business logic in components; typed data services
  • Typed reactive forms; server-side validation too
  • Feature routes lazy-loaded; bundle budgets enforced in CI
  • No method calls in template bindings on hot paths
  • bypassSecurityTrust* audited (file 13 §4.1)
  • Accessibility: semantics, labels, keyboard, contrast, live regions
  • Loading, empty, and error states designed for every async view

🔍 Interview angles

  • How does Angular change detection work, and what does OnPush change? Zone.js patches async APIs and triggers a tree-wide check; OnPush restricts checking to reference-changed inputs, local events, async-pipe emissions, and explicit markForCheck — signals make it fine-grained and enable zoneless.
  • switchMap vs mergeMap vs concatMap vs exhaustMap? Cancel-previous / all-concurrent / queue-in-order / ignore-while-busy. Give the typeahead and double-submit examples.
  • Why did my list re-render everything? Missing track/trackBy, or a new array identity with recreated objects.
  • Signals vs RxJS? Values vs streams. Signals for synchronous derived state and templates; RxJS for time-based and cancellable async. Bridge with toSignal.
  • How do you avoid memory leaks? async pipe, takeUntilDestroyed, shareReplay with refCount, unsubscribing from third-party listeners, and cleaning up effects.
  • How would you speed up a slow Angular page? Measure first (Angular DevTools profiler + Lighthouse), then: OnPush/signals, track, virtual scroll, @defer, remove template method calls, lazy-load routes, shrink the bundle, and check whether the real cost is actually the API.
  • interface vs type? Interfaces merge and are better for object contracts; type aliases handle unions, intersections, and mapped types. Either is fine — be consistent.
